items.title: Snow Brings Austria to a Halt
items.gist: A heavy November snowfall covered Vienna and disrupted travel across the country. Some roads closed, and officials warned that cold weather could keep the snow in place.
items.summary: Vienna recorded 17 centimetres of snow at the Hohe Warte weather station on Thursday. ORF reported that the city had not seen this much November snow in more than 40 years. The A21 motorway was closed for several hours. Accidents and delays were also reported in Lower Austria, Carinthia and Tyrol. Weather experts said the snow may remain because freezing conditions are expected.
items.host_open: Vienna got a very early winter blanket, but the roads paid the price. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Calls for a New Prosecutor’s Office Plan
items.gist: Legal experts have criticised a draft law on Austria’s planned federal public prosecutor’s office. The debate centres on how independent the office would be from politicians.
items.summary: Austria is discussing a draft for a federal public prosecutor’s office. Legal experts say the proposal could give parliament influence over appointments. They also warn that parliament could oversee the office while investigations are still under way. Supporters of the draft argue that the new body needs democratic oversight. Critics say safeguards are needed to protect its independence. ORF reported calls for a fresh start to the proposal.
items.host_open: A new prosecutor’s office needs both independence and public trust. What matters most to you in this debate?

items.title: Universities Seek Budget Talks
items.gist: Staff at Austria’s public universities want the government to reopen budget discussions. They say funding for the years ahead needs another look.
items.summary: Employees at Austria’s 22 public universities held workplace meetings on Wednesday. They called for new talks on the universities’ budget for 2028 to 2030. The request comes as institutions plan their work for the coming years. University staff say funding must match their needs. The government has not yet announced a new negotiation timetable. The issue matters for research, teaching and university jobs.
items.host_open: Universities are planning years ahead, while their budget still needs discussion. What do you think deserves priority?

items.title: Trump and NATO Chief Discuss Russia
items.gist: Donald Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte urged Russia not to widen the war in Ukraine. Their meeting comes as European leaders discuss Ukraine’s future funding.
items.summary: Trump and Rutte met at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida. They called on Russia not to expand its war in Ukraine and said a peace solution was needed soon. The war continues to shape security debates across Europe. EU leaders are also discussing Ukraine’s financing needs for 2027. The meeting did not announce a new peace agreement. Russia’s position was not included in ORF’s report.
items.host_open: Calls for peace are coming alongside continued fighting. How do you feel about that?

items.title: Israeli Strikes Kill People in Gaza
items.gist: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed ten people, according to an Associated Press report. The violence continues despite a ceasefire deal reached more than a year ago.
items.summary: The Associated Press reported that Israeli strikes killed ten people in Gaza on Thursday. The report said Israeli fire and airstrikes have continued almost daily despite a ceasefire deal. The AP said it could not independently verify some claims in its coverage. The latest deaths add to the human cost of the conflict. The report also described wider regional tensions, including Iranian drone attacks in Kuwait. Further details about the victims and the circumstances were limited in the report.
items.host_open: More people have been killed despite the ceasefire agreement. How does this news make you feel?

items.title: EU Leaders Clash Over Long-Term Budget
items.gist: EU leaders are meeting in Brussels to discuss the bloc’s next seven-year budget. Disagreements remain over its size and how to fund Ukraine’s needs.
items.summary: Leaders of the European Union met in Brussels on Thursday and Friday. They are discussing the long-term budget for 2028 to 2034. Ukraine’s financing needs for 2027 are also on the agenda. The EU Council president said he hoped to bring countries closer to agreement. Several governments object to parts of the proposed budget. The talks matter because the EU needs agreement from all member states on the plan.
items.host_open: Europe’s next budget has to balance many competing priorities. What should leaders focus on first?

items.title: Spain’s Former Central Bank Chief Chosen for ECB
items.gist: EU leaders have chosen Spain’s former central bank head to lead the European Central Bank next. The institution faces difficult choices on inflation and government borrowing costs.
items.summary: EU leaders selected Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next president of the European Central Bank. He previously led Spain’s central bank. He is set to succeed Christine Lagarde, according to the Associated Press. The ECB is dealing with inflation and concerns about government debt and borrowing costs. The report linked price pressures partly to the war in Iran. The appointment still needs to proceed through the relevant EU process.
items.host_open: A new ECB president will face tough choices on prices and debt. What do you think should be the main priority?

items.title: Judge Blocks Early ABC License Review
items.gist: A US judge has stopped the regulator from starting an early review of ABC’s broadcast licences. The network argued that the move threatened its freedom to report and speak.
items.summary: A federal judge in Washington blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC’s broadcast licences. ABC had argued that the move could chill its free-speech rights. The network welcomed the ruling as a First Amendment victory. The decision came after tensions between the government and the broadcaster. The ruling is about the regulator’s attempt to review licences early. It does not end wider disputes over media regulation.
items.host_open: A court has drawn a line in a dispute over media oversight. Did that surprise you?

items.title: ORF Approves Its 2027 Budget
items.gist: The ORF supervisory board has approved the broadcaster’s budget for 2027. The plan includes measures to offset a loss of federal funding.
items.summary: ORF’s supervisory board approved the broadcaster’s budget for 2027 on Thursday. ORF said it plans steps to make up for a financial shortfall from the federal government. One of the planned measures is a 40-million-euro package. The budget decision sets the broadcaster’s financial framework for next year. The report did not provide full details of all planned savings or measures. The funding question matters for Austria’s public broadcaster and its services.
items.host_open: The ORF has set its budget for next year while facing a funding gap. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Thanksgiving Turkey Becomes Political News
items.gist: The annual turkey-pardon ceremony drew fresh attention in Washington. Late-night coverage focused on President Trump’s questions about choosing the turkey.
items.summary: President Donald Trump took part in the annual Thanksgiving turkey-pardon ceremony. News coverage said he appeared confused about how to size up a turkey. The ceremony is a White House tradition before Thanksgiving. Seth Meyers discussed the moment in a recent segment, according to coverage of his show. The event is light-hearted, but it also provides a regular opportunity for public political jokes. The turkey was pardoned as part of the tradition.
items.host_open: Even the Thanksgiving turkey ceremony became a sizing-up exercise. Did that surprise you?
